title: Searches return Hits and no function takes a config struct
body:
Callers configure and query through option structs. `SearchOptions`, `CountOptions`, `ExtractOptions`, `ListOptions` and `LocateOptions` and their result types live in `libsufr/src/types.rs` (`SearchOptions` at 211, `LocateOptions` at 475). The builder has three ways to set the sort: `with_sort_type`, `with_max_query_len` and `with_seed_mask` (`sufr_builder.rs:143-152`). `max_query_len` and low memory are passed per query.

The CLI handlers in `sufr/src/lib.rs` hold logic that belongs in the library.

- `locate`: sort and group hits per sequence (480-526).
- `extract`: absolute coordinates and a second `string_at` call per hit (385-405).
- `summarize`: building 15 or 16 labelled rows (569-642).
- `parse_locate_queries`: treating a path as a query file (439-457).
- `count`, `extract` and `locate` share one skeleton, including the `Box<dyn Write>` choice and `very_low_memory ? true : low_memory`.

## Proposal

- `SuffixArray::open(path)` and `open_with(path, Load::{Memory, Subsampled(mql), Disk})`.
- `sa.search(b"ACG")` returns `Hits`. `Hits` has `count()`, `ranks()`, `locate()` and `extract(before, after)`.
- `SuffixArrayBuilder` takes `.sort(Sort::Full | MaxQueryLen(n) | Mask(m))` and drops the three older setters.
- The option and result structs are deleted. No function takes a config struct.
- The CLI-resident logic above moves into the library. `-l`, `-v` and `-m` map onto open options, and CLI output does not change.

The unmerged `search-api` branch has a similar query model (`SuffixArray::open`, `search -> Hits`). It is the inspiration, not a spec. It has 12 conflict hunks in 5 files against the current builder.
